title: A Coworker Chat About Staying Calm During a Tense Meeting
script: Sari: [concerned] Yoga, are you okay? You looked like you wanted to walk out of that meeting halfway through.
Yoga: [tense] Honestly, I was one comment away from saying something I would have regretted immediately afterward.
Sari: [curious] What set you off so badly? You usually handle criticism better than almost anyone else on our team.
Yoga: [frustrated] When the director blamed my department for the delay, although the real problem started with the supplier weeks before that.
Sari: [understanding] That does sound unfair, especially since you warned everyone about the supplier issue back in March.
Yoga: [tense] Exactly. So when he said it in front of the whole company, I felt my face getting hot immediately.
Sari: [gently] What stopped you from correcting him right there, in front of everyone in that meeting?
Yoga: [thoughtful] I remembered something my old mentor told me once: never respond to public criticism with public anger, because both sides lose.
Sari: [interested] So what did you do instead, if you didn't say anything during the meeting itself?
Yoga: [calmly] I breathed slowly, wrote down my thoughts on paper, and waited until the meeting had completely ended before saying anything at all.
Sari: [curious] Did you talk to him afterward, once the meeting was over and everyone had left the room?
Yoga: [honestly] Yes, privately, in his office. I explained the timeline calmly, with the emails to support what I was saying.
Sari: [interested] How did he react once you showed him the actual timeline and those emails?
Yoga: [relieved] He apologized immediately and said he would clarify the situation with everyone at our next weekly meeting.
Sari: [warmly] That's a much better outcome than if you had argued with him in front of the entire company today.
Yoga: [reflective] I know. If I had reacted angrily, he probably would have defended his position instead of actually listening to mine.
Sari: [smiling] Well, I'm proud of you for handling that so well. It clearly wasn't easy for you to stay quiet today.
Yoga: [grateful] Thanks, Sari. Honestly, my hands were still shaking a little under the table the entire meeting.
